judgements.justification: B's Reviewer_456H based its 4 on two wrong claims (a 25-step sweep reveals the map, though stone and water zones block it; executor training explains the near-oracle gap, though the oracle shares the executor); A's Reviewer_1PbL wrongly said the paper compares 'only to ablations'.

B's AC gave a spotlight with no reviewer above 7 and none asking for an award, on its own view that the paper is 'pretty cool' and an 'exemplar', and wrote that consensus 'clearly shifted towards a mean of 7' over ratings 7, 4, 7, 7.
No praise-only low-confidence review: A's champion aK3Q was the most careful reviewer (confidence 5, 11 h, ran the code), and B's 7s were at confidence 4 with specifics.
No flaw was disclosed on one forum only; the authors confirmed the full-map training on both forums.

B learned from DgEc and 456H that the executor trains on full-map programs and the hallucinator on true states, yet its meta-review did not weigh this and stated the method does not depend on ground-truth programs, true at test time only.
After the rebuttal A's Reviewer_EBwR lowered 6 to 5 when the authors declined the neural-controller run, while B's Reviewer_DgEc rose to 7, so score movement in opposite directions widened the gap.
Only A raised baseline strength (128/32-unit MLPs, Relational below End-to-end), a neural controller over the same options, the TAMP framing, and the AC's POMCP and TD-VAE; no one in B raised these.

Both committees saw privileged full-map training, user-supplied state abstraction, small static grids and the same presentation slips; A's kENU and EBwR held them against the paper while B's reviewers rated 7 and SkvM called the clarity points minor.
Neither AC adopted one reviewer's position: A's AC added its own novelty objection, and B's AC followed three 7s and its own enthusiasm.
No reviewer is recorded as moving because of the other reviews.
The authors answered each reviewer; 1PbL, not the authors, left the request to name unclear parts unanswered, and EBwR's drop came from a declined experiment, not a misreading.
A's Reviewer_Wt3P gave 4 after four clarification questions, named no flaw, never replied, and its rating counted among A's four below-threshold scores.
A's majority was negative (4, 4, 4, 5 against one 7), so its reject did not go against a positive majority.
Neither AC stated a positive view while deciding by a mean threshold; A's AC was negative and B's AC went above the scores.
The low scores rested on clarity, privileged training and baselines, which are central to the contribution, not peripheral points.
Both committees read the paper as program synthesis over hallucinated worlds and praised that idea; A's task-planning framing point is a missed-literature issue, not a different kind of contribution.
No reviewer who disclaimed expertise raised on the rebuttal; DgEc's raise came at confidence 4 with no stated reason.
Neither committee demanded a deliverable of this paper type that the other did not; the differences lie in weighting and in issues raised.
No reviewer's praise rested on a wrong claim; the wrong 'no privileged information' statement came from B's AC in the meta-review, which R05 covers.

A's Reviewer_kENU conceded 'I stand corrected' on the program-synthesis baselines and was 'more confident that the baselines are good' after new runs, yet kept 4 on clarity and saying the changes 'warrant a complete re-review'.

A's kENU refused to credit the rebuttal's new runs and promised changes, saying they 'warrant a complete re-review', while B accepted the new non-deterministic and explore-then-plan runs and the promised related-work fix.
DgEc's mismatch runs the other way: it edited its rating to 7 but its text still argued against acceptance and it posted no comment, so no stated stance diverged from an unchanged score.
Neither AC called in an off-record extra reviewer.
Clarity verdicts split, but the notes do not tie them to reviewers' distance from the field; A's confidence-5 aK3Q called the writing very clear while confidence-3 reviewers did not.

added.name: Reviewer raised score silently against own text
added.definition: A reviewer in one committee raised their rating after the rebuttal with no stated reason while their review text still argued against acceptance, and the committee counted the raised rating.
added.justification: R22 covers a stated change of stance with an unchanged score; here the score changed and the text did not. R06 covers rebuttal-driven score moves but not a raise with no reason that contradicts the reviewer's own text.

added.name: Area chair set aside a silent detractor
added.definition: One committee's area chair discounted a low rating because its reviewer did not respond to the rebuttal or discussion, so the decision followed the remaining reviewers, while the other committee counted a comparable unengaged rating.
added.justification: R12 covers an unengaged review that counted unchallenged; no reason covers the opposite step, an AC removing an unengaged detractor's rating from the decision.

reasoning: The two committees mostly saw the same facts and weighted them differently (R08), with A-only issues on baselines, framing and the AC's uncited POMCP and TD-VAE (R07). Reviewer draw and the ACs separated the outcomes: A counted a thin silent 4 (R12) and kENU kept 4 after conceding points and refusing to credit revisions (R20, R21); B's lone 4 rested on misreadings (R01) and was set aside by the AC (new R26), DgEc rose silently to 7 against its own text (new R25), and the AC chose a spotlight above the scores while misstating the privileged-training point (R02, R05). Rebuttal moves went in opposite directions (R06).
